title: The constructible inner model

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 87–88 (§20, Lemmas 20.5 and 20.7, Corollary 20.8 and Theorem 20.9; axiom witnesses, minimality, idempotence and Choice, with the recorded definability-parent-stage repair); revision 2026-01-31

summary: Verify every ZF axiom in L using reflection and construction-stage bounds, then build coherent internal well-orders to prove Choice and minimality.
abstract: Iterating definable subsets produces a transitive class containing every ordinal, but each set-theoretic axiom still needs witnesses inside that class. For the constructible class L, finite-family reflection turns a definition using truth in the whole class into a definition over one set level. Bounding the construction stages of a set of outputs then supplies Replacement and the internal power set, which collects precisely the constructible subsets. These arguments verify every ZF axiom. Transitive-model agreement of the hierarchy shows that constructing inside L gives L again and that every inner ZF model contains it. Finally, a recursion orders each old level before its newly definable objects, comparing the latter by least formula-and-parameter codes over the already ordered level. Those well-orders exist internally, proving that L satisfies Choice as well as ZF without assuming ambient Choice.
